items.summary: We present flash-comm, a communication library that achieves efficient transport for LLM decoding by fusing readiness synchronization with data movement. flash-comm introduces self-synchronizing transfers in which each data block carries evidence of its readiness, allowing receivers to directly validate the blocks they need without separate inter-GPU barriers. items.title: TestBED: An Open-Source Toolkit for Bayesian Experimental Design
items.summary: Bayesian experimental design (BED) is a principled framework for intelligent data acquisition with applications across a wide range of scientific and industrial domains. However, the development and adoption of BED remains hindered by a lack of standardised software and benchmarks. Existing methods are typically implemented in bespoke codebases and evaluated on a small subset of tasks, making methods difficult to apply, compare, or extend. items.summary: New simulations by researchers at the Simons Foundation’s Flatiron Institute and the University of Texas at Dallas show that intense ultraviolet light acted like a cosmic leaf blower, pushing gas and dust away from stars in the early universe and making their galaxies appear brighter.

items.summary: The matrix mortality problem asks whether a given finite family of matrices can be multiplied, in any order and with possible repetition, to get the zero matrix. items.summary: We investigate positive solutions with both components nontrivial for systems of Hammerstein integral equations associated with a general $2\times2$ matrix of Green's kernels, thereby extending the decoupled (diagonal) case to systems with cross-coupling. items.summary: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. items.summary: Automated program reduction shrinks a program into a smaller one that preserves a property of interest. Language-agnostic grammar-based reducers are easy to retarget across languages, but because they reason only about syntax, they cannot perform the coupled edits needed to remove whole declarations, e.g., a method cannot be deleted while it is still called. items.summary: Early assessment of Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) vectors from Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) can reduce the delay between initial public disclosure and official National Vulnerability Database (NVD) scoring. items.summary: Loop closure detection conventionally cascades separate models for global retrieval, geometric verification, and relative pose estimation, leading to redundant computation and disconnected visual representations. items.summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single model. Such a loss of orthogonality manifests as cross-basis leakage onto user-allocated chirp subcarriers, which we characterize by…

items.title: Research on gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of Schwarzschild spacetime
items.summary: We investigate gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Its angular component is described by a two-dimensional Randers space, with the Schwarzschild limit recovered at Finslerian parameter $ε= 0$. This structure breaks spherical symmetry, causing generic orbits to undergo orbital plane precession. Using multipolar radiation reaction and adiabatic orbital averaging, we derive the leading order Finslerian corrections to the…

items.title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?
items.summary: We view a $k\times n$ Latin rectangle as $n$ points in the grid $[n]^k$. Each symbol gives one point, whose coordinates are the columns it occupies. The rectangle is balanced when these points are pairwise equidistant in the $\ell_1$ metric. Its imbalance measures the distance from this ideal. We study the minimum imbalance from three sides. items.title: The enhanced polylogarithm conjecture in weight two for imaginary quadratic fields
items.summary: Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture predicts that special values of Dedekind zeta functions can be expressed in terms of polylogarithms at algebraic arguments. For imaginary quadratic fields, Zagier and Gangl refined it by lifting both sides to complex values modulo rational multiples of a power of $2πi$. items.title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series forecasting is critical for demand prediction and resource management in modern Web services, yet applying pretrained Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) to downstream tasks remains challenging due to domain shifts. Existing retrieval-augmented approaches typically retrieve coarse-grained window contexts and may introduce context-specific noise. To address this problem, we argue that temporal patterns should be reused at a decomposition level, as effective trend and seasonal dynamics may originate…

items.title: Linear adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. items.title: Gravitational-Wave Microlensing as a Probe of Compact Object Population
items.summary: The abundance of compact objects ranging from stellar to intermediate masses ($\sim 1 - 10^{5}M_{\odot}$) remains poorly constrained, particularly for populations such as primordial black holes and dark matter subhalos that emit little or no electromagnetic radiation. Gravitational-wave (GW) microlensing provides a complementary way to probe these populations through wave-optics effects imprinted on the GW signals, with implications for astrophysical and cosmological inference. We develop a hierarchical Bayesian…

items.title: DecoupAttn: Decoupled Sparse Attention for Training-Free Acceleration of Video Diffusion
items.summary: Sparse attention accelerates few-step video diffusion transformers by computing a few key blocks exactly and compensating for the rest. However, existing sparse attention still faces key challenges, including identification overhead from finding critical blocks at every denoising step, suboptimal budget allocation that sets sparsity budgets uniformly or by local metrics, and cross-step error accumulation as reused masks or clusters go stale. Observing that the errors left on skipped blocks cancel each other once…

items.summary: As sequence lengths continue to grow, distributed attention based on sequence parallel (e.g., Ring-Attention) has become a mainstream solution for large language models (LLMs). Nevertheless, inherent communication dependencies limit computation-communication overlap, reducing GPU utilization. Moreover, in cross-hardware (NUMA or node) architectures, due to imbalanced communication bandwidth, frequent communication synchronization will limit overall performance. items.title: A Rankin-Selberg Integral for $SU_{2,2}$
items.summary: We construct a Rankin-Selberg integral for the non-split quasi-split unitary group $SU_{2,2}$ and prove that it is Eulerian. We then compute the local integral at inert places where all data are unramified, and show that it represents the local adjoint $L$-function of $SU_{2,2}$.

items.title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
items.summary: We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble converges for each $β>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $β$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrtβ$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu.

items.title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
items.summary: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. items.title: Variational exponential estimates and stationary large deviations for SPDEs
items.summary: We establish an abstract criterion for large deviations of invariant measures when the deterministic dynamics has a single globally attracting equilibrium. Deterministic regularisation and attraction yield an endpoint estimate for long controlled paths of bounded action, uniformly over each fixed bounded initial set. This allows the finite time Freidlin-Wentzell uniform LDP on bounded initial sets to be combined directly with stationary exponential norm estimates. items.title: Energy exchange confined to the perturbations: the frozen dark sector confronted with Planck, DESI, supernovae and cosmic shear
items.summary: We present cosmological constraints on the frozen model, in which dark matter and dark energy exchange energy only at the level of the perturbations. The expansion history is that of flat $Λ$CDM, while on sub-horizon scales a dimensionless coupling $Σ$ enhances ($Σ<0$) or suppresses ($Σ>0$) the growth of the dark-matter density contrast. items.summary: We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. items.title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
items.summary: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes. Here, we present an \textit{in situ} dual-enhancement mechanism to address these bottlenecks without requiring external site-specific fine-tuning. items.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
items.summary: Neural operators fit their representation of functions to the task they are trained on, so every new task rebuilds a reduced space from labeled data. Following the self-supervised pre-training that made representations shareable in natural language processing and computer vision, we decouple representation learning from operator learning. A functional autoencoder is pre-trained on analytic functions synthesized on the fly, with no solver and no labels, to represent functions on arbitrary point clouds, and the…

items.title: Rheology and Velocity Distribution of Couette Flow for Protoplasmic Streaming
items.summary: We investigate two-dimensional Couette flow between parallel plates as a model of protoplasmic streaming in plant cells using a combined Langevin and Navier?Stokes simulation. The interaction between the fluid and biological materials is implemented using a Finsler geometry (FG) modeling technique, in which the interaction strength, represented by quantities such as relative viscosity, effectively varies with an internal degree of freedom (IDOF) associated with the biological materials. items.summary: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. items.title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
items.summary: We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. items.title: The Galois actions on braided fusion categories
items.summary: This note harmonizes two classical topics: minimal modular extensions of braided fusion categories and the Galois action on modular fusion categories. Their common generalizations are Galois-modular extensions, which always exist when a braided fusion category $\mathcal{B}$ is pseudounitary. Each extension induces a Galois action on the simple objects of $\mathcal{B}$. items.title: Quadratic reset bounds for finite maximal prefix codes
items.summary: Let $C$ be a finite maximal prefix code of maximum codeword length $k\ge2$. We prove that, whenever the literal decoder of $C$ is synchronizing, it has a reset word of length at most $(k-1)(4k-5)$. The bound is independent of the alphabet and the number of decoder states. Its main ingredient is a short-detection theorem: a linear observation of the decoder, with terminal weight constant on states of depth $k-1$, is either identically zero or nonzero on a word of length at most $2k-3$. items.title: A motivic Vojta inequality for non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded height
items.summary: We study a bounded-degree form of a motivic Vojta inequality for pure André motives, arising from a question of Kato. We verify this inequality for infinitely many non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded stable Faltings height. The point is that ramification at the finite poles of the $j$-invariant gives the required discriminant bound.

items.title: AQUA - A Modular Authentication Quality Modeling Framework
items.summary: Authentication solutions are the key design, architectural, and implementation decisions that implement authentication security controls. An example is a password-based authentication solution. While researchers often examine authentication quality, existing approaches do not distinguish which effects on quality stem from which aspect of authentication. items.title: Quaternionic Wave Numbers and the Dirac Equation: Resolving the Nielsen--Ninomiya Barrier and Infinities
items.summary: We exemplify the applicability of the rational wave numbers by formulating the relativistic Dirac equation on the discrete sequence space $\mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}$ over the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$ and demonstrating how this resolves fundamental issues relating to Dirac's equation. items.title: Multimodal Fusion Methods for Whole-Slide Images and Clinical Data in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: Multimodal AI fusion of histology and clinical data is an active research area in computational pathology, but fusion methods are rarely compared under identical conditions and across different clinical endpoints. We present a modular framework in which slide-level embeddings, obtained by training an attention-based aggregator over patch embeddings from a frozen foundation model, and per-visit clinical embeddings are fed into 15 interchangeable fusion methods with a shared output dimension and prediction head…

items.title: Readable Is Not Steerable: Pre-Registered Tests of Physical Structure in Learned Fluid Representations
items.summary: Self-supervised world models are often said to organize their latents around physical quantities. We test this on 2D decaying Navier-Stokes flow in three pre-registered studies, each tested once on held-out data. In Study 1, a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) trained to predict the flow fails the pre-registered criteria for organizing its latent around fluid quantities better than an untrained network of the same architecture (not supported); a JEPA trained on non-physical linear dynamics and a…

items.title: PrimordialPy: A Python library for single-field inflation, primordial black holes, and scalar-induced gravitational waves
items.summary: We present \texttt{PrimordialPy}, an open-source Python library designed to compute the cosmological predictions of arbitrary canonical single-field inflationary models. By numerically solving the background dynamics and the curvature perturbation equation, the package evaluates the primordial power spectrum of scalar and tensor perturbations at all relevant scales. Furthermore, it automatically computes the resulting mass fraction and abundance of Primordial Black Holes (PBHs), as well as the associated spectrum…

items.title: Energy-efficient End-to-End Communication System with Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: 2030 is expected to witness the first commercial 6G systems. However, traditional modular communication architectures cannot meet the latency, optimisation, and integration requirements demanded by various sub-millisecond, data-intensive emerging 6G applications. End-to-end (E2E) communication addresses these limitations by replacing traditional processing blocks with neural networks. Nevertheless, conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) in E2E systems use dense computation. This results in substantial…

items.title: ProofStudio: Five Proof Assistants in the Browser
items.summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted proof automation are extending the use of proof assistants in software verification and mathematics. However, greater proof automation does not remove users' responsibility to assess whether formal statements capture their intended requirements, making education in formal specification and reasoning essential. To lower the installation and learning barriers associated with mature proof assistants, we present ProofStudio, a browser-based environment integrating Isabelle/HOL, Lean…

items.title: Constraining the Milky Way Mass profile with data driven distribution function using DESI DR2 halo stars
items.summary: We employ a novel data-driven dynamical modeling method, the empirical distribution function (emPDF), to constrain the Milky Way mass profile using a large sample of halo stars from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Milky Way Survey (DESI MWS). The method does not assume any functional form of the tracer distribution. items.title: Mock catalogues for the DESI DR2 Milky Way mass modeling effort
items.summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) survey is an ongoing campaign to obtain millions of spectra, including for stars within the Milky Way. One of DESI's Key Projects for its second data release (DR2) is to measure the mass of the Milky Way using a variety of techniques applied to six-dimensional kinematics of distant halo stars. We present mock surveys generated from the Auriga cosmological simulations (AuriDESI) that are used to validate these techniques in several companion studies. The AuriDESI…

items.title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
items.summary: We present measurements of the mass of the Milky Way using distant halo stars selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2). We apply four dynamical modeling methods to 10,036 RR Lyrae (RRL) and blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars with 6D phase space coordinates that span from $\sim$10 to 95 kpc from the Galactic center, the largest samples of their kind. items.title: ReveaLLAGN 2: Exploring the Nuclear Gas and Stellar Kinematics of Nearby LLAGNs with JWST/NIRSpec IFU
items.summary: Low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGN) represent the most common mode of black hole accretion in the local Universe, yet their nuclear structure, stellar and gas kinematics remain poorly constrained at parsec scales. We investigate the nuclear regions of eight nearby representative LLAGN, the ReveaLLAGN sample: M87, M104, M94, M81, NGC1052, NGC4258, NGC5128 and NGC4395. items.title: Superconducting Qubits as Quantum Targets for Direct Particle Scattering
items.summary: We introduce a novel approach to particle detection in which a superconducting qubit itself serves as the scattering target and a resolved transition between circuit eigenstates constitutes the observable final state. The scattering amplitude factorizes into the incident-particle current and a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition response of the qubit. items.title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
items.summary: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. items.title: Dynamically modulated light-matter interactions for ancilla-tolerant bosonic control

items.summary: We consider the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on the cable system of a transient weighted graph with volume growth exponent $α$ and Green function decay exponent $ν$. items.title: Gepner stability conditions on hypersurface categories
items.summary: We construct numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the category of graded matrix factorizations of every smooth complex projective hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$. These conditions are of Gepner type $(τ,2/d)$, where $τ$ is the grading shift autoequivalence. items.summary: Let $Y$ be a smooth cubic 3-fold. We show that $S^2 \times Y$ admits an infinite sequence of cohomologous symplectic forms which are all deformation equivalent but pairwise non-isotopic; McDuff showed the corresponding result on $(S^2)^2 \times T^2$, but these appear to be the first simply-connected and monotone examples. items.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction

Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. items.title: A note on cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
items.summary: K. Broder recently classified the closed Einstein 4-manifolds whose isometry groups have dimension at least three. The proof reduces the problem to the study of cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics invariant under $SU(2)$, however a few cases are not treated. We reconcile the missing cases using Broder's techniques with minimal modifications.

items.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks

items.summary: We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.

items.title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking
items.summary: Tracking-by-propagation (TBP) methods perform end-to-end multi-object tracking by propagating track queries across frames, jointly handling detection and identity association without heuristic post-processing while naturally modeling temporal information. items.summary: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. items.summary: We investigate the cosmological dynamics of axion-monopole interacting dark energy, examining whether a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can sustain stable late-time acceleration. items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely deployed in modern machine learning. items.summary: The ability of mechanical systems to perform basic computations has gained traction in recent years, providing a robust supplement to digital computing in off-grid, low-power, and extreme environments where electronics are inaccessible or risk failure. However, prior work has focused on Boolean logic applied via bistable structures, snap-through mechanisms, or origami lattices. items.title: A Smooth Shioda-Tate Isomorphism for Elliptically Fibered 4-Manifolds
items.summary: This paper studies a subgroup of the mapping class group of an elliptically fibered $4$-manifold $π: M\to B$, inspired by number theory. items.title: PadLoc: Training-Free Floor-Plan Localization by Sparse Geometric Matching
items.summary: We propose PadLoc, a training-free localization back-end that places a moving sensor within a known floor plan. items.summary: Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. items.summary: We prove a quantum analogue of the classical moment matching method, a popular framework used to prove lower bounds in property testing. For two random variables $X_0$ and $X_1$ whose moments match up to the first $r-1$ moments, the classical moment matching method says that no classical algorithm can reliably distinguish between input instances of length $N$ constructed from $X_0$ and $X_1$, respectively, unless it performs at least $Ω(N^{1-1/r})$ queries. items.summary: Quantum error correction provides the mathematical basis for protecting quantum information against noise. Existing formalizations have established foundations for stabilizer codes and code verification. items.summary: Pervasive Capability Degradation (PCD) refers to the phenomenon in which supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while adapting a large language model (LLM) to a target task, often erodes the general capabilities acquired during pre-training. items.summary: Separate compilation is central to modular software: components are compiled independently and linked into an executable. Separate compilation is correct when a linked program behaves like the program formed by merging its sources. This property is less routine to prove than type soundness because it requires a formal account of linking. items.summary: We investigate the automated generation of executable robot reinforcement learning (RL) policies from natural-language task descriptions. Rather than using large language models (LLMs) as execution-time decision makers, we use them as designers that construct RL pipelines before deployment, including Markov decision process (MDP) formulation and simulator implementation. items.summary: This work proposes, implements, and evaluates a modular architecture based on software design patterns applied to latency measurement in Software-Defined Networks (SDN) using the Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and the Express Data Path (XDP). items.title: Current control of spin-wave transport in YIG via the $\small\mathbfVO_\mathbf2$ insulator-to-metal transition
items.summary: Electrically reconfigurable spin-wave transport is central to realizing energy-efficient magnonic information technologies, yet existing current-driven approaches require current densities that undermine the fundamental dissipation advantage of spin-wave-based signal processing. items.summary: Complex visual question answering often requires vision-language models to think with images, i.e., actively acquire local visual evidence by zooming into informative regions of high-resolution images. items.summary: We study optimal contracts when an agent allocates continuous effort subject to polymatroid capacity constraints. Effort produces a linear expected reward and incurs a cost. items.summary: Charge-Parity Violation (CPV) is expected in three-body charm decays. items.summary: The annual modulation reported by the DAMA/LIBRA collaboration remains in tension with the null results of other direct-detection experiments. items.summary: Leakage-resilient cryptography protects secrets against side-channel attacks, in which a physical implementation reveals partial information about its internal state. A fundamental primitive in this area is a leakage-resilient storage, which allows a secret to be stored in a way that remains secure even if an adversary learns some information about the storage's internal state. items.summary: We study derived Ringel duality for modular category $\mathcal O$ on downward-closed, quasi-bounded supports. items.summary: We compare genus zero degree two Gromov--Witten invariants with the number of embedded conics on general projective complete intersections whose conic space has expected dimension zero. items.title: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models
items.summary: Among 291 surveyed open-weight language model repositories (280 distinct embedding tables), 52.6% of untied gated and hybrid checkpoints (20/38) contain reachable input embeddings with norms below $10^{-6}$, compared with 0% of weight-tied models. Such near-zero rows can arise during pretraining when unseen rare or template tokens receive zero input gradients while AdamW weight decay shrinks untied embeddings. In tested Transformer configurations, non-initial positions or a BOS token prevent this failure mode. In…

items.title: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness
items.summary: We present an approach to mathematically formalizing PTX, an approach that allows modeling and reasoning about patterns common in GPU kernels for Deep Learning, including acquire-release, tensor cores, proxies, async operations, multi-kernel pipelines and data-dependent control flow. We implement it in Lean and use it to prove the correctness of simple implementations of a WGMMA GEMM kernel, FlashAttention, and a 3-kernel MoE pipeline.

items.title: Annealing-Induced Structural and Optical Evolution of Ion-Beam-Sputtered Ta2O5 Films for High-Power Laser Applications
items.summary: Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) thin films deposited by ion beam sputtering (IBS) are essential components in high-power laser systems, where post-deposition annealing is routinely used to optimize film quality. In this work, we systematically investigate the structural and optical evolution of IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers subjected to post-deposition annealing at temperatures from 400 to 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The films undergo an amorphous-to-polycrystalline transition between 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and…

items.title: SWAP-INR: Implicit Neural Representation with Switchable Attention Paths for Time-varying Multivariate Scientific Data Compression
items.summary: Visualizing multivariate scientific simulation data is essential for understanding complex physical phenomena, yet the massive scale of such data imposes a severe storage bottleneck in high-performance computing environments. Implicit neural representations (INRs) have emerged as a promising continuous alternative to traditional lossy compressors, but existing methods struggle to explicitly capture cross-variable interactions and to adapt to the diverse spectral characteristics of physical variables. To address…

items.title: LiquidCP: Decoupling Attention Tasks from Communication and Kernel Boundaries in Context Parallelism
items.summary: Context parallelism (CP) partitions long sequences across GPUs for LLM training and inference. For variable-length training and full prefill, attention-balanced placement can leave token loads uneven, while ring execution repeats overhead at each computation and communication step. In stage-serialized decode CP (DCP), long-running tasks delay dependent work and leave substantial GPU hardware idle. We propose LiquidCP, which unifies training and inference through a common model of Transfer, Compute, and Reduction…

items.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
items.summary: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide a strong starting point for deployment, but adapting them to a target robot and environment still requires costly embodiment-specific demonstrations. Human demonstrations are far easier to collect, yet directly leveraging them is challenging due to the substantial human-robot embodiment gap, particularly when the underlying VLA has been pretrained primarily on robot data. We introduce H2RB (Human-To-Robot Bridge), a human-robot co-training framework for…

items.title: The smallest-parts function and elliptic curves
items.summary: Recently, Ono established a new connection between partition congruences and the arithmetic of elliptic curves by expressing the partition function $p(n)$ as a CM trace on the modular curve $X_0(6)$. This approach yields new proofs of Ramanujan-type congruences for the partition function modulo powers of $5$, $7$, and $11$, revealing how the geometry of supersingular elliptic curves and the arithmetic of oriented optimal embeddings govern these congruence properties. Motivated by Ono's work, we develop an…

items.title: Monodromy Computation Model
items.summary: A closed path can return to its starting point while analytic continuation reaches another branch. We construct a finite computational calculus in which retained logarithmic branches supply memory, analytic observations select operations, and descent through a covering exposes deeper memory. Three branch coordinates suffice, and every finite observation uses the same cubic power covering. Each program defines a globally real analytic return map whose integer-lattice execution is realized by actual path lifting…

items.title: IGSW: Multi-Weather Urban Scene Reconstruction with Intrinsic-Decoupled Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: High-fidelity weather editing of 4D scenes can support end-to-end training and closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving. Combining generative image editing with dynamic Gaussian representations enables multi-weather scene reconstruction, but weather-edited images often contain structural distortions. Directly fitting their appearance may propagate errors from teacher images into the reconstructed 4D scene, compromising the original scene structure and temporal continuity. To address these challenges, we…

items.title: RH-Conditional Positivity in a Theta-Kernel Langevin Model
items.summary: A classical Brownian-bridge representation of Riemann's xi function defines an even, rapidly confining probability density and a reversible Langevin model. Our principal physical observable is the transient variance after a quadratic-potential quench; we also analyze a tilted bridge-range response and a sixth-order cumulant gap. For a specified passive harmonic trap with bounded delayed residual feedback, we derive a non-vacuous finite-time variance-increase bound under explicit calibration and sampling…

items.title: Asymptotic electromagnetic transition conditions for thin layers: the arithmetic-mean field and susceptibility hybridization
items.summary: Effective transition conditions that replace a thin polarizable layer by a zero-thickness sheet are commonly applied in electromagnetic models of two-dimensional (2D) materials and metasurfaces. These conditions usually take the arithmetic mean of the fields on either side as the polarizing field at the boundary, and characterize the layer by the $0^\mathrm{th}$ moment of its susceptibility, but both choices are typically imposed rather than derived. We derive transition conditions for a finite-thickness…

items.title: Measuring the ultraviolet background at $z\simeq3$ from the quasar proximity effect in DESI DR1
items.summary: Ionizing radiation from quasars reduces the abundance of neutral hydrogen in the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM), suppressing Ly$α$ absorption. This absorption deficit, known as the quasar proximity effect, can be used to measure the ultraviolet background (UVBG). We measure the hydrogen photoionization rate of the UVBG in Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Our sample contains 6,245 quasars over $2.75\leq z<3.25$, selected with rest-frame absolute magnitudes at 1450…

items.title: Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions
items.summary: The simultaneous determination of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and fundamental physical parameters, e.g. the strong coupling constant $α_s$, the mass of the top quark $m_t$, or Wilson coefficients of an Effective Field Theory operators, is essential for the high-precision physics programme of the Large Hadron Collider. Yet, simultaneous global fits face significant methodological and computational challenges, rooted in the fundamental tension between estimating a finite-dimensional parameter and an…

items.title: ReuseGR: Offline--Online Decoupled Generative Retrieval via Adaptive Prefix Reuse
items.summary: Larger generative retrieval models can improve retrieval quality, but their decoding cost makes low-latency serving difficult. When different users submit the same query, generating complete Semantic IDs (SIDs) for every request repeats computation, while their interaction histories call for different results. The challenge is to reuse large-model computation across requests while keeping retrieval personalized. We propose \textbf{ReuseGR}, which separates query-level candidate planning from request-level…

items.title: Novel hydrodynamic features in dissipative spin-polarized fluids
items.summary: We investigate an extension of perfect spin hydrodynamics that includes dissipation in the spin sector. The presence of dissipation implies that antisymmetric parts of the energy-momentum tensor should be taken into account. Their form follows from the Navier-Stokes or Israel-Stewart theory, which introduces a priori unknown kinetic coefficients and relaxation times. We find that the inclusion of the antisymmetric parts of the energy-momentum tensor has twofold effects: i) they form source terms for the spin…

items.title: UMLoad: Fast On-Demand Model Loading on Unified Memory Architecture
items.summary: On-demand model loading dominates response latency for interactive on-device AI, yet unified memory architectures (UMAs), now common on edge devices, should make it cheap by placing weights in memory the GPU already sees. However, frameworks still use the loading flow built for discrete GPUs, leaving significant inefficiencies. This paper presents UMLoad, a system-level model-loading accelerator that decouples a framework's logical allocations from their physical page backing. UMLoad uses on-demand reconstruction…

items.title: Observable gravitational waves from unstable ALP catastrogenesis
items.summary: We focus on gravitational waves (GWs) observable in pulsar timing array and interferometric searches that are produced by the annihilation of cosmic string-wall networks in axion-like particle (ALP) models. We called this process "catastrogenesis." It produces GWs with a characteristic peaked spectrum. These GWs would not be observable if the ALPs were stable. We thus assume that ALPs decay into two photons before Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). The large ALP-photon coupling required could induce field…

items.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
items.summary: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

items.title: Friedman--Stanley cofinality without Borel completeness
items.summary: Friedman and Stanley asked whether an invariant Borel class of countable structures must be Borel complete whenever every countable level of their hierarchy reduces to it. We construct a counterexample in one fixed countable language. The structural counterexample and its principal supporting results have been formalized in Lean~4 and it is available on github.

items.title: Higher zeroes in pointed infinity-categories
items.summary: We construct an endofunctor on (small) simplicial sets which freely adjoins a zero object to a (small) infinity-category, as the co-cone construction freely adjoins a terminal object. We then prove that this endofunctor induces a left adjoint to the inclusion of the infinity-category of (small) pointed infinity-categories and morphisms that preserve zero objects into the infinity-category of (small) infinity-categories. This adjunction, in turn, leads to the definition of a coherent choice of nullhomotopies on a…

items.title: Say the Same, Act Differently: Diagnosing and Steering Text-Action Divergence in Reasoning VLAs
items.summary: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models pair physical control with natural-language rationales that supervisors can read to monitor embodied safety. Prior attacks on VLA reasoning corrupt the rationale itself and leave visible evidence in the text. We show that visual perturbations can instead alter the physical action while keeping the generated rationale word-for-word identical. At the shared text/action interface of Alpamayo for driving and InstructVLA for manipulation, our text-neutral action-subspace…

items.title: The Arc Threshold of the Two-Row Ising Torus: Exact Factorization, an Algebraic Critical Coupling, Uniformity in the Circumference, and the Rate of Convergence
items.summary: The Lee-Yang circle theorem places every zero of a ferromagnetic Ising partition polynomial on the unit circle. The arc condition, that every zero lie in the closed left half-plane, turns the circle theorem into a product formula for the characteristic function of the occupation count and makes it usable for local limit theorems. For the two-row periodic Ising torus we give the exact reflection factorization of the row transfer matrix, reduce the crossing at zeta = i to a real cubic, and identify the critical…

items.title: Infinite-Horizon Stochastic Recursive Differential Games with Jumps: Nonautonomous Coefficients and Nonzero Terminal Values
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate a class of decoupled infinite-horizon forward--backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) with time-dependent coefficients and jumps. Under suitable time-integrability conditions on the coefficient growth and stochastic Lipschitz moduli, we establish an $L^p$ theory ($p\ge 2$) for these systems, including well-posedness, moment estimates, conditional stability, and tail estimates, without imposing dissipativity of the forward dynamics or monotonicity of the backward…

items.title: PhotonZip: Lifecycle-Aware Compression for HDF5-Based Synchrotron Workflows
items.summary: Synchrotron detectors generate data at rates that challenge storage and I/O systems. Compression can reduce data movement, but codec-only measurements do not capture the end-to-end behavior of HDF5 workflows. We present PhotonZip, a lifecycle-aware compression framework that tests candidate modes through a common HDF5 path and selects among eligible measured configurations according to either compression ratio or round-trip throughput. Its modular filters preserve standard HDF5 access when the required plugin is…

items.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
items.summary: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.

items.title: GINsim 3.1: Qualitative modelling and dynamical analysis of logical regulatory networks
items.summary: GINsim is a software for the definition and dynamical analysis of qualitative (Boolean and multi-valued) models of biological regulatory networks. Building on its modular architecture, based on the MDDlib decision-diagram and bioLQM model-manipulation libraries, GINsim version 3.1 introduces new functionalities aimed at the analysis of large logical models: the symbolic computation of trap-spaces, the Booleanisation of multilevel models and the reversal of model dynamics. GINsim 3.1 also extends the estimation of…

items.title: Glauber dynamics of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model: a dynamical cavity method
items.summary: We present a closed theory, exact in the $N\to\infty$ limit, of the equilibrium spin correlations of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model evolving with Glauber dynamics, above and at the transition temperature $T_c$. The derivation uses a dynamic cavity approach: in the evolution equation for the selected spin the other spins are represented by a fluctuating field. The influence of the selected spin on this field is included at the linear response level; it is given as a sum of the spin's past flips…

items.title: Query-based Submodular Data Selection for Efficient Instruction Tuning
items.summary: As large language models are fine-tuned for increasingly specialized tasks, their performance depends more on which training examples are selected than on how many. Given a large heterogeneous training pool and a small target set specifying the desired capability, targeted data selection aims to find a compact subset that maximizes downstream performance. Existing methods score each candidate independently against the target and select the top-ranked examples, yet this point-wise strategy ignores inter-example…

items.title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
items.summary: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $ρ$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some…

items.title: Controlling Action-Head Co-Adaptation to VLM Representation Anisotropy
items.summary: Modern learning systems increasingly combine pretrained models with downstream heads. Despite the growing importance of such modular designs, how the downstream model co-adapts to the geometry of pretrained representations remains relatively underexplored. We study this problem through vision-language-action models (VLAs), where a pretrained vision-language model (VLM) conditions an action model for control. We find that the action model progressively concentrates its sensitivity on high-variance dimensions of…

items.title: Adaptive Qubit Encoding for Continuous-Variable Quantum Optimization
items.summary: Optimizing continuous-variable functions on qubit-based quantum hardware requires a finite representation of the search space and a solver-compatible representation of the objective function. Fixed-grid discretizations provide a direct encoding, but restrict the search to a predefined range and resolution; at the same time, constructing a compact Hamiltonian for a general continuous-variable objective can be impractical. Here, we introduce a framework for continuous-variable optimization tailored to qubit-based…

items.title: A Ghost-Free dS/AdS Correspondence in $\mathcalN=1$ Supergravity
items.summary: Reversing the sign of the scalar potential exchanges de Sitter and anti-de Sitter vacua and, through the domain-wall/cosmology correspondence, maps flat domain walls onto flat FLRW cosmologies, but its supersymmetric version has ghosts on the cosmological side. We show that this pointwise correspondence is realized between two ordinary, ghost-free four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravities with spontaneously broken supersymmetry. Within a single superconformal Kähler cone, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ reflection of the…

items.title: Hydrogen Electron Cyclotron Resonance Dissociator Demonstrator for the Project 8 Experiment
items.summary: Project 8, a neutrino mass experiment, employs the novel frequency technique of cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (CRES) to perform a model independent measurement of neutrino mass via tritium beta decay. Our pioneering experiment will consist of a beamline that dissociates molecular tritium, surface cools atoms through accommodation, evaporatively cools and slows atoms, and traps them in a CRES resonant cavity to advance towards our sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2 for our final electron-weighted neutrino…

items.title: A Modular Open-Source Python Framework for Small Satellite Attitude Determination and Control
items.summary: Advanced attitude determination and control (ADCS) techniques can be difficult for small satellite teams to adopt: tightly coupled implementations require substantial code changes to evaluate different actuators, sensors, orbits, mission goals, and control laws. Existing tools often emphasize orbit mechanics or flight software rather than closed-loop ADCS. This paper presents an open-source, modular ADCS framework in pure Python for rapid development, repeatable testing, and flight-oriented integration across…

items.title: OpenAI Conference at KITP
items.summary: There was a conference held at KITP the week before last entitled Intermediate-Scale AI for Physics. The nature of this conference was somewhat of a mystery. As far as I can tell it never appeared in the list of forthcoming … Continue reading →

items.title: We Ran a Research Sprint With AI. The AI Worked. The Research Didn't
items.summary: Generative AI tools for research are widely deployed, yet individual productivity gains do not guarantee better team research. We argue that how AI use is structured matters alongside access. Personal AI tools may amplify two failures under deadline pressure: a consumption bottleneck, in which generation outpaces team-visible evaluation, and AI-induced research silos, in which private human-AI loops displace shared decision-making. We motivate this position with a mechanism-generating pilot: a 100-minute research…

items.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over sextic fields
items.summary: We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $6$. Apart from the $44$ groups that occur infinitely often, which were determined by Derickx and Sutherland, exactly four groups occur: $\mathbb{Z}/25\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$. The first three were known to occur, while the group…

items.title: Modular and Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search with Vectorium and kANNolo
items.summary: Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) search over neural embeddings powers modern retrieval systems such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Embeddings come in three representations (dense, sparse and multi-vector), and efficient search combines an index structure, a similarity function and a quantization scheme. Existing libraries fix one combination, hard-code each one separately, or factor only one side of the problem, and none covers all three representations. We present Vectorium and kANNolo, two open-source…

items.title: Noisy pipelines II: Non-parametric Noise Inference for LISA
items.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to observe gravitational-wave signals from massive black hole binaries, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and more. Despite the significant scientific potential, accurately extracting these signals from the data will only be possible if LISA's instrumental noise is understood: poor noise modelling will result in lost signals, biased parameter estimates, and incorrect astrophysical insights. Modelling LISA's instrumental noise is more challenging than its…

items.title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
items.summary: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every…

items.title: On the lower- and upper bounds of three-colored anti-Ramsey numbers
items.summary: In this paper we study a relatively new Ramsey type graph parameter introduced by my Bachelor's thesis supervisor Nóra Almási, and her Master's thesis supervisor Maria Axenovich. The parameter $ξ(G)$ denotes the largest natural number $n$, such that there is a red-blue-green edge coloring of $K_n$, such that in the edge coloring all copies of $G$ represent all three colors. After a brief recap on Ramsey numbers, we precisely define $ξ(G)$, and take a look at its relations to the Ramsey numbers. In the third…

items.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Large foundation models often answer even when the available visual or textual evidence is insufficient to support a reliable conclusion. This failure to abstain makes them hard to trust in high-stakes or information-seeking settings, where a confident but unsupported answer can be worse than no answer at all. It also raises a natural question: can the internal mechanisms behind this behaviour be identified and controlled at inference time? We present Dr. No, a feature-steering approach that mines sparse…

items.title: One-Sided Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators on Variable Lebesgue Spaces Beyond Log-Hölder Continuity
items.summary: We study the boundedness of the right-sided Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over the real line. Motivated by the $K_0$ condition for the classical Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator, we introduce a directional condition $K_0^+$ adapted to the geometry of the one-sided maximal operator. We characterize $K_0^+$ in terms of the uniform boundedness of a family of one-sided averaging operators and prove that it is a necessary condition for the boundedness of $M^+$ on…

items.title: Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow
items.summary: We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not scalar-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in[0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient…

items.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
items.summary: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is…

items.title: Compact holography via polarized IKKT
items.summary: The polarized IKKT matrix model is a $U(N)$ supersymmetric matrix integral proposed to be dual to an $N$ D-instanton sector of Euclidean type IIB string theory. We show a direct path from matrix model saddles to supergravity saddles: matrix model resolvent $\to$ holomorphic function $\to$ 2D Coulomb potential $\to$ 4D Coulomb potential $\to$ supergravity fields, where the last step was previously described. Here, the 2D electrostatics picture is an exact finite $N$ reformulation of a localization deformation of…

items.title: A Sojourn Through $c=1$ String Theory
items.summary: We revisit the $S$-matrix, the thermal $S$-matrix and the thermal free energy of $c=1$ string theory from the worldsheet perspective. By numerically integrating Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants, we compute the scattering amplitudes and thermal amplitudes up to 6-point at tree level and up to 3-point at one loop, in addition to the genus two thermal free energy. All results are in agreement with the predicted answers from the $c=1$ matrix model.

items.title: Cosmic-Ray Signals from Dark Matter Annihilation into Scalars with Baryon Number
items.summary: Cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium-3 nuclei are promising probes of dark matter (DM). In light of potential detections of heavy antinuclei at AMS-02, we investigate a recently proposed scenario in which DM annihilates into color-singlet scalars carrying baryon and lepton number, which has been shown to enhance antideuteron and antihelium-3 fluxes relative to antiprotons. Accounting for Galactic propagation and detector sensitivities, we calculate the number of events predicted by our model for parameters…

items.title: 3D dark matter map of the JWST COSMOS-Web field using diffusion-based generative priors
items.summary: Mapping the three-dimensional distribution of dark matter is key to tracing the growth of cosmic structure. Two-dimensional weak lensing mass maps recover its projected distribution, but they blend structures at different distances along the line of sight. We reconstruct the three-dimensional matter distribution in the 0.54 deg$^2$ COSMOS-Web field using deep James Webb Space Telescope imaging, with an effective source density of 121 galaxies arcmin$^{-2}$ We combine a physical weak lensing forward model with a…

items.title: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
items.summary: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of…

items.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
items.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they…

items.title: Cyclicity of Drinfeld modules modulo primes in arithmetic progressions
items.summary: Let $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $K=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$, and let $φ$ be a Drinfeld $A$-module over $K$ of rank $r\geq 2$. We study the reduction of $φ$ at primes $\mathfrak{p} \in A$ lying in a prescribed arithmetic progression, for which $φ(\mathbb{F}_{\mathfrak{p}})$ has at most $r-1$ cyclic components. We obtain asymptotic formulas for the number of such primes of a given degree, with error bounds uniform in the modulus of the arithmetic progression. Furthermore, when $\mathrm{End}_{\overline K}(φ)=A$, we sharpen the…

items.title: Synchronization of Enriched Spin Glasses
items.summary: We show that enriching a non-convex multi-species Hamiltonian by a uniform Ruelle probability cascade implies synchronization of the joint overlap array without an additional regularizing perturbation. In particular, we show that any limit point of the overlap array is a deterministic non-decreasing function of a uniform Ruelle probability cascade.

items.title: Nonlinear gauge maps and the structure of Goldstone loops in canonical inflation
items.summary: We clarify the nonlinear relation between the spatially flat scalar and Goldstone descriptions of canonical single-field inflation. An exact clock map shows how potential interactions are reorganized into derivative Goldstone interactions. A change of slicing further connects their dilation symmetry to its comoving realization. We then study the Goldstone two-point function at one loop in the decoupling limit. Using identities derived from the general mode equation, we reveal how seemingly independent loop…

items.title: GW/PT-correspondence for CY $4$-fold-II: Virtual Classes
items.summary: Let $B$ be a complex manifold and $f:\bX\to B$ a derived \textit{complex-analytic} (not necessarily \textit{algebraic}) space with an oriented relative $(-2)$-shifted symplectic structure. We suppose that the closed symplectic form is locally exact in the completed relative de Rham complex, and construct a derived smooth manifold over $B$, independent of additional choices. When $f$ is proper and oriented, this gives integral virtual fundamental classes on its fibres. Our argument is heavily based on the strategy…

items.title: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
items.summary: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a…

items.title: Haagerup symmetries of the $E_8$ theory and conformal nets at central charge eight
items.summary: A Haagerup algebra is a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight with $\mathrm{Rep}(U)$ braided equivalent to the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category. We prove that $U$ has exactly three holomorphic extensions, each isomorphic to $V_{E_8}$, and that the corresponding Lagrangian algebras have module categories $\cal H_1$, $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$. The extensions attached to $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ are the two lattice extensions of $V_{E_6 \oplus…

items.title: Lecture note on Fourier decoupling theory and its applications
items.summary: This paper is based on lecture notes taken and organized during the 17th Graduate Mathematics Intensive Training Program (Spring 2025), held at the Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research, in which Professor Shaoming Guo lectured on "An Introduction to Fourier Decoupling Theory." The main content includes an introduction to and proofs of $\ell^2$ decoupling inequality, together with its applications in number theory, harmonic analysis, and geometric measure theory. The writing follows Professor…

items.title: An information-geometric formulation of distributed computation
items.summary: Understanding how complex systems perform computations, i.e. how they store, transmit, and transform information across their components, is a major goal across the natural sciences. However, characterising genuinely collective computations across multiple inputs and outputs that cannot be reduced to contributions from individual components remains an open problem. In this work, we introduce $Φ\text{ID}^{IG}$, a geometric theory of information dynamics that captures irreducible collective phenomena and enables a…

items.title: Rank stability of elliptic curves over prime cyclic extensions of function fields
items.summary: Let $\ell$ be an odd prime number. Let $E$ be a non-isotrivial elliptic curve defined over the global function field $K = \mathbb{F}_q(t)$ such that $(q, 6) = 1$ and $q \equiv 1 \mod \ell$. We show that as $q$ grows arbitrarily large, both analytic and algebraic ranks of $E$ do not grow upon base change to $100\%$ of $\mathbb{Z}/\ell \mathbb{Z}$ Galois extensions over $K$. One of the applications we obtain is that over a positive proportion of $\mathbb{Z}/\ell \mathbb{Z}$ Galois extensions $L$ over $K$, the…

items.title: Stability of negative-regularity mixing and applications to stochastic fluids
items.summary: We consider mixing for a scalar advected by random vector fields, such as solutions to stochastic fluid equations. Our main abstract result is that contraction in expectation of a negative Sobolev norm of the scalar (negative-regularity mixing) is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process. items.title: Theory of the Ferroaxial Charge Density Wave in 1T-TiSe$_2$
items.summary: Recent experiments using strain to probe the charge-density wave (CDW) of 1T-TiSe$_2$ have uncovered additional transitions and broken symmetries inside the CDW state. The elastocaloric effect reveals a second transition below $T_\mathrm{CDW}$, which elastoresistivity shows to be associated with ferroaxial order, breaking all vertical mirror symmetries while preserving inversion. items.title: Zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields
items.summary: We calculate zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields using the classification of Tits and prove a functional equation. We give explicit exam- ples of these zeta functions for non-split unitary and orthogonal groups.

items.title: Grid-Mode-Aware AI Data Center Power Smoothing via Bayesian-Optimized Hybrid Energy Storage System
items.summary: AI data centers exhibit highly stochastic, volatile power demands from intensive workloads and synchronized GPU training cycles, which can excite grid natural frequencies and threaten system stability. This paper proposes a real-time, forecasting-independent control framework utilizing a Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) that coordinates a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) and a supercapacitor (SC). Employing a parameterized frequency-decoupling and active modal-damping policy, the framework mitigates…

items.title: Circumventing Magnitude Collapse via Modular Two-Stage Open-Set Recognition
items.summary: Open-set recognition (OSR) requires neural networks to classify known classes while rejecting unknown samples, which is critical for real-world deployment. So far, OSR research studied and developed representation learning and postprocessing methods independently and their interactions remain unexplored. In this paper, we reconsider OSR as a modular two-stage pipeline and present the first systematic study of interactions between representation learning and postprocessing methods across dataset scales and usage…

items.title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
items.summary: Deep learning models for electronic health records achieve strong predictive performance but provide little insight into what clinical concepts they represent internally. Post-hoc attribution methods produce per-cell importance scores that lack temporal coherence, cross-variable structure, and reusability across patients. items.summary: Global tractography offers a theoretical framework for reconstructing white matter connectivity from diffusion MRI by jointly inferring all streamlines and their consistency with the diffusion signal and underlying anatomical priors. items.summary: Geometric duality reveals a novel bridge between a series of well-known scalar effective field theories: the Yang-Mills theory coupled to a specific scalar sector (aka the Yang-Mills-scalar theory), the nonlinear sigma model on a symmetric coset space, the Dirac-Born-Infeld theory, and the special Galileon theory. items.title: A Note on the Finite-Exceedance Dependence Principle for Sum--Maximum Asymptotic Independence
items.summary: Asymptotic independence between sum-type and maximum-type statistics arises repeatedly across many areas of probability and statistics, particularly in high-dimensional testing and random matrix theory. Motivated by the shared structure underlying existing proofs, which is obscured by their model-specific formulations, this note isolates a common intermediate principle. items.title: Quaternionic and Octonionic Frameworks for Quantum Computation: Mathematical Structures, Models, and Fundamental Limitations
items.summary: We develop detailed quaternionic and octonionic frameworks for quantum computation grounded on normed division algebras. Our central result is to prove the polynomial computational equivalence of quaternionic and complex quantum models: Computation over $\mathbb{H}$ is polynomially equivalent to the standard complex quantum circuit model and hence captures the same complexity class BQP up to polynomial reductions. items.title: Smoothing the Bouncing-Geodesic Singularity in AdS/CFT
items.summary: Black hole singularities remain a central open problem in quantum gravity. In the AdS/CFT correspondence, bulk spacelike extremal surfaces can probe the black hole interior, and information about the near-singularity geometry is encoded in analytically continued boundary correlators. As the bouncing geodesic approaches the black hole singularity, it becomes nearly null and gives rise to characteristic divergences at complex times. items.title: Algebraic Characterization of Time-Varying Set Invariance
items.summary: The verification of temporal forward invariance for dynamical systems subject to time-varying constraints is a foundational problem in the analysis of safety-critical systems. Existing methodologies rely on restrictive geometric assumptions, such as the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ), or suffer from exponential computational complexity when applied to time-varying polytopes. This paper establishes a rigorous, unified, and computationally tractable framework for temporal safety verification…

items.title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
items.summary: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. items.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. items.summary: We apply Functional Dimensional Regularization (FDR) to the Lee-Yang universality class, a paradigmatic non-unitary theory, and compute its main critical exponents across the dimension range $1\leq d\leq 6$. By combining a second-order derivative expansion with polynomial field expansions, we obtain results that are compatible with resummed $\varepsilon$-expansion as well as with state-of-the-art estimates from Conformal Bootstrap, Fuzzy Sphere and Non-Perturbative Renormalization Group. items.title: Free energy of the Hopfield model
items.summary: We identify the limit of the free energy of the Hopfield model with independent symmetric Bernoulli patterns, for every temperature and loading ratio. A Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation reduces the problem to that of identifying the limit free energy of a bipartite spin glass with $\pm 1$ and spherical spins. items.summary: Let F be a field, G = GL_n(F), and let St be the Steinberg module of G. For a parabolic subgroup P of G, let St_P be its Steinberg module. There is a natural map rho_P: St -> St_P corresponding to intersection of a modular symbol with the Borel--Serre boundary. We construct a ZP-resolution Sh_P of St_P, the P-sharbly resolution. items.title: Pod-wise Multimodal Federated Learning for Heterogeneous IoT
items.summary: Federated learning (FL) is well suited to Internet of Things (IoT) sensing. However, devices carry different sensors and come online in periodic patterns, and as such, the sensors among the participants change from round to round. Under naive averaging, devices without a sensor overwrite its parameters, and a single-sensor device never learns how its sensor relates to the others. Existing methods either redesign local training for mismatched sensors (assuming always-available devices) or select clients without…

items.title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
items.summary: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. items.title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization has emerged as a promising approach for memory-efficient large language model (LLM) post-training, yet its reliability in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) remains largely unexplored. Motivated by the distinct data regimes of on-policy RL and fixed-data optimization, we develop a generic variance-theoretic framework to investigate what limits the reliability of ZO gradient estimation. items.title: Poisson Super Learning For Survival And Competing Risks On A Discretized Time Scale
items.summary: We introduce the Poisson Super Learner, a scalable ensemble method for survival and competing risks prediction with right-censored data. The approach exploits the correspondence between the likelihood of piecewise-constant hazard models and the Poisson likelihood. This raises a fundamental question: how much dissipation we need to ensure global stability and decay? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $φ$ such that no primary lighter than $φ$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. items.summary: Laminar-turbulent transition governs skin friction, heat transfer and losses in turbomachinery, yet Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) transition models rely on empirical correlations and hand-calibrated activation functions whose structural deficiencies cannot be resolved by recalibration. items.title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
items.summary: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. items.summary: We study anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory for self-dual twists of $p$-ordinary modular forms of weight two with nebentype $ε^2$, where $ε$ is a non-trivial Dirichlet character of conductor $p$. items.summary: We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. items.summary: Spherical transformer configurations can accelerate grokking through simultaneous modifications of several model properties. The present study investigated the contributions of these modifications in the published Sphere+Fourier configuration using 960 controlled modular-arithmetic runs. items.summary: LLM post-training via reinforcement learning has shown consistent improvements in accuracy at the cost of reducing behavioral coverage - a phenomenon known as sharpening that can stall progress on difficult tasks. Repeated sampling objectives such as $\mathrm{pass@k}$ and $\mathrm{max@k}$ are known to mitigate sharpening, but the mechanism behind it remains poorly understood. items.title: Regularity of core coupled high-spin structure in neutron-rich $^{196-202}$Au isotopes approaching N $=126$

items.title: From Simulation to Sustainable Urban Mobility: A Purpose-Driven Framework for Advanced EV Charging Technology Transfer
items.summary: The integration of electric vehicles (EVs) into urban mobility systems offers both opportunities and challenges for cities pursuing sustainability and energy efficiency. While simulation-based approaches have demonstrated the technical feasibility of advanced charging strategies, such as smart charging, bidirectional charging, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G), their real-world impact is often constrained by policy, business models, and stakeholder engagement. items.summary: Spatial audio has an accessibility problem. Largescale spatial and immersive audio installations remain costly and exclusive, with high barriers to entry. We propose ''Ananas,'' a networked audio system consisting of network protocols, control software and microcontroller firmware, with the aim of rendering spatial audio applications accessible to a broad cohort of potential users. items.title: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts
items.summary: Complex video editing requires understanding complex instructions while jointly fulfilling multiple editing requests. Meeting these demands through dense model scaling substantially increases computational cost. We introduce VideoEditor-MoE, the first open-source mixture-of-experts framework for video editing. items.summary: Design thinking is widely taught as an iterative loop of ideation, prototyping, and testing, yet conditions under which such a loop must improve innovation outcomes remain unspecified. Taking problem framing as given, we formalize the iterate-test core as search over a finite prototype space whose utility is learned through noisy evaluations. items.summary: We construct smooth, strictly positive solutions of the three-dimensional cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials whose densities become unbounded in finite time. A main ingredient is a new velocity weight that is Gaussian on a ball and has a polynomial tail of fixed order. items.summary: We study real zeros of completed modular L-functions and the determination of cusp forms by their periods. items.summary: An agent that explores, whether it generates conjectures or research ideas, must decide which of them are worth keeping. items.title: Gibbs Variational Last Layers for Long-Horizon Dynamics Learning
items.summary: Accurate long-horizon probabilistic predictions of dynamical systems are a prerequisite for model-based decision-making.
